t: This is St Stephen Walbrook, next to the Mansion House, near Bank and Monument stations. The domed church was designed by Sir Christopher Wren after the Great Fire of 1666 destroyed its medieval predecessor. Wren was given responsibility for rebuilding fifty-two City churches, and his masterpiece is St Paul's Cathedral. The church takes its name from Saint Stephen, the first Christian martyr. Buried here are Sir John Vanbrugh, the architect of Blenheim Palace and Castle Howard, and the physician Nathaniel Hodges, who wrote an account of the Great Plague. Benjamin Winthrop, a Governor of the Bank of England, is also buried here.
